newsitem.title: UK: UK grain futures active, down on sterling strength.
newsitem.headline: UK grain futures active, down on sterling strength.

text.p: LIFFE grain futures fell in active trading on Wednesday as the market reacted to sterling's strength against other European currencies.
Prices were dictated entirely by currency, traders said.
"There's still a sense that it's fundamentally bearish," one said. But he noted that talk in the market was more about what sterling was likely to do than fundamental grains news.
Wheat volume was healthy, bumped up by trades out of front month March into, in particular, May.
May was most active, with 524 of the total 957 lots traded, followed by March, with 208 lots.
Shipper selling took November to 134 lots, traders said.
May last traded 0.95 stg down at 94.75 stg.
Barley also fell. Of a total 11 lots, 10 were on November, which last traded 0.50 stg lower at 92.50 stg.
